messages.content: Hi tal, I'm a friend

hey, i'm tal

think of me as your personal talent agent, your inside man… or fox

one of these days, I might slide a role right here in chat. the kind that feels like your calling.

so… what's your full name?
Krutika

krutika... that's a solid name with some serious energy behind it

where you working these days?
Google. I'm an account manager in the ad sales team

google ad sales... selling the machine that prints money for the internet. respect.

found krutika phadke - dft engineer at google on linkedin. this you? https://in.linkedin.com/in/krutika-phadke-445977188
No

my bad... let me try again

found kritika joshi - google ads account manager at wns. this you? https://in.linkedin.com/in/kritikajoshi313

or can you just drop your linkedin url? easier that way
My full nane is kk krutikashri
there we go... k k krutikashri - growth at google, ex-sprinklr, cbs'23. this you? https://in.linkedin.com/in/krutikashri
Yes

cbs'23 to sprinklr to google growth... that's a solid trajectory from campus to scaling the world's biggest ad engine. what made you jump from sprinklr to google? better growth opportunities or just tired of the startup grind?

fair point on sprinklr... they're definitely past the startup phase. my bad.

so you want to flip from growth/sales to the other side of the table - either funding startups, building products, or sitting in founders' ears. that's a solid pivot but very different paths.

vc is relationship-heavy, product is execution-heavy, and eir is chaos-heavy. which one actually gets you excited when you think about doing it day-to-day?

also... how long you been working total?

2.5 years and already plotting your escape from google... respect for the ambition.

product and vc both make sense with your growth background. you've seen what moves the revenue needle, which is gold for product decisions. and for vc, you understand how businesses actually scale beyond the pitch deck fantasies.

what kind of role you looking for next - junior product roles, analyst positions in vc, or going straight for the eir chaos?

<caption></caption>
    <analysis>{
  "transcription": "Analyst positions in VC.",

analyst track it is... smart move. easier to break into vc as an analyst than trying to jump straight to principal level.

bangalore or open to remote/other cities?

<caption></caption>
    <analysis>{
  "transcription": "open to any city in India or the world but I would not want to work remote.",
  "language": "English",

  "backgroundSounds": "None"
2.5 years experience + vc analyst roles + any city but no remote... sound right?
done. i'm spinning things up on my end. you'll start seeing good stuff soon.

yooo you're in! 🎉

here's the deal - i'm gonna slide vc analyst roles right into this chat when they match your vibe. no spam, just actual opportunities at funds that are worth your time.

networking tip while we're here: forget linkedin cold messages. start writing about deals you find interesting, share hot takes on startup trends. vcs notice people who think, not people who ask for coffee chats.

now go build that vc brain while i hunt down some solid analyst positions for you 🔥

twitter for vc brain, linkedin for vc jobs. vcs live on twitter for deal flow and hot takes. linkedin is where they post job openings.

start with twitter - follow 10 vcs you admire, engage with their threads, share your own takes on deals you find interesting. quality over quantity.

got it - vc analyst roles first, but i'll keep an eye out for founders office and faang non-tech roles too. you're basically looking for anything that gets you closer to the startup ecosystem or big tech strategy.

my team will ping me with anything that fits that mix. you'll see them pop up here when they do.

Cool
  What did you use to build the product? Bery interesting

my source code is my therapist's problem... but i'm good at what i do. that's all you need to know.

so... career stuff?
Yes

Yes
  Thisss

perfect. so you're looking at vc analyst roles, founders office, and faang non-tech - all while building your twitter presence for vc networking.

what's your timeline for this shift? actively looking or just exploring?

actively looking - got it. i'll ping you when my team sends something that matches your vc analyst/founders office/faang non-tech mix.

in the meantime, start following vcs on twitter and engage with their deal analysis threads. that's how you get noticed.
Can you share some VCS I can follow?

start with indian vcs: rahul chowdhri (stellaris), anand lunia (indiaquots), avnish bajaj (matrix), shanti mohan (letsventure). follow their deal threads and engage thoughtfully.

also follow global vcs who invest in india: sequoia india, accel india, lightspeed india. watch how they analyze startups.
Thanks
welcome. ping me when you land your first vc analyst interview.
Hi
Any job warm opening

nothing warm yet... but i'm scanning thousands of roles daily. when something fits your vc analyst/founders office/faang non-tech mix, you'll see it pop up here.

in the meantime, how's the twitter vc networking going?
Nice! Just replied to d couple of vc's post today

nice! that's exactly how you get noticed. keep it up - thoughtful replies, not just "great post!" energy.

anything specific you're looking for in those vc analyst roles? early-stage funds vs growth equity? specific sectors you're interested in?
Sector agnostic

sector agnostic - good. early-stage funds will give you more deal flow experience, growth equity more financial modeling. both valuable.

what's your current salary? helps me filter for roles that actually make sense financially.
1.5 lakhs roughly a month

got it. ~18 LPA at google growth. vc analyst roles at early-stage funds might be lateral or slight bump depending on the fund size. growth equity/founders office roles could offer more.

what's your target comp? helps me filter for roles that actually make sense.
2 lakhs + bonus and stuff

2 lakhs/month + bonus is realistic for vc analyst roles at decent funds. founders office roles at well-funded startups could hit that too.

i'll keep an eye out. anything else i should know about your search? location preferences beyond "anywhere"?

hey - perplexity (the ai search startup) is hiring a strategic finance lead

they specifically want 2+ years of vc/pe/strategic finance experience

comp is ~1.6-1.9 crores, works directly with product and growth teams

what do you think?

saw a strategic finance role at perplexity - hot AI startup

they specifically want 2+ years in VC/PE/strategic finance, which is rare

comp is 1.6-1.9 crores, way above your target. SF location though

hey, happy monday - if it’s not, we’ll work together on making it happen soon :)
how’s the week looking? what would you like me to focus on this week with the search?
